name: container_layers
description: Give the effective view of a container's layers from the layer directories alone, without starting a container or mounting overlayfs: for each path, which layer supplies it and what each layer did to it (added, replaced, deleted, made opaque, present but hidden). The layers come as `layers` (directories of extracted layer trees from the base to the top, with an optional `upper`, the writable layer) or as `overlay2_root` with `start` (overlay2's own storage: `start` is a layer directory name, its `lower` file lists `l/<short id>` links that are resolved inside overlay2_root and nowhere else, to ../<id>/diff). A lower layer that cannot be resolved is `missing` and listed (the chain is then cut and the status is partial), a lower entry that is not an overlay2 short id is another layout and is listed, a chain that repeats a layer is a loop and is not followed, more than 4096 layers are refused, and a link in a layer is listed and never followed (a link loop costs nothing). The view is built from the top layer down: a path is supplied by the topmost layer that has it unless a higher layer deleted it or made a directory above it opaque. OCI whiteouts (a file `.wh.<name>`, and `.wh..wh..opq` in a directory) are told apart from overlayfs native ones (a character device with device number 0/0, and the xattr trusted.overlay.opaque or user.overlay.opaque = y on a directory); extraction often loses the xattr and may not create devices, so each layer says whether its extended attributes could be read here, how many native whiteouts and opaque directories were found, and `opaque_directories_not_told_in_layers` names the layers with native whiteouts whose attributes were not readable: a directory that was opaque there cannot be told from an ordinary one and its lower contents may show as visible. Each row of the view (pages.view, one per path, ordered by path) has the path, whether it is visible, the layer that supplies it (counting from the base), its type, size, mode and modification time, and the changes layer by layer; `path_prefix` keeps one subtree (a filter over shown text). Bounds: 200,000 entries per layer, 500,000 paths in all, 512 path components and the clock every 256 entries; a layer or view past a bound is named and the status is partial; max_seconds (default 60, at most 105, under the manifest's 120) is honoured and the layers below the one being read are then not read (partial). Names are the layers' own bytes (a name that is not UTF-8 is shown as an escape). It reads no file's content, so a secret in a file is not seen; `copy: true` with `copy_paths` names up to 1000 effective regular files (each at most 64 MiB, 512 MiB in all) to copy to $OUT/layers-view/<path>, only in a job run as secret output (declared secret_output: a job that sets copy is run as secret output, and the tool refuses it outside a job or when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1), never over a file that is already there (a taken name is not replaced: the same bytes are named again and a different file takes the next free name), through a hidden temporary name; a path that is deleted, hidden, a directory or a link is reported as not copied. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP ends the tool with one JSON last word (status failed, exit 128 plus the signal) naming the paging file it had written, and an unexpected exception ends it with one JSON document and exit 1. A file, a link or any entry that is not a directory in a higher layer hides everything a lower layer holds under that path (those rows are present_but_hidden and are never copied). The `start` of overlay2_root and the names in a lower file may not be `.` or `..`, and a link to a place outside the store is not followed. The clock is read while the view is built and listed. It does not reconstruct layers from image manifests, read other storage drivers (overlay v1, aufs, devicemapper, btrfs, zfs) or follow redirects and metacopy of overlayfs.

layers.description: Directories of the layers from the base to the top (up to 4096), each a real directory; not with overlay2_root

upper.description: With layers: the container's writable layer directory, applied on top of the others

start.description: With overlay2_root: the name of the layer directory to start from (a container's mount id, or an image layer's cache id); its lower file gives the chain

path_prefix.description: Keep only this path and what is under it in the view (a plain path inside the layers, no leading / and no ..)

copy.description: SENSITIVE: true copies the effective files named in copy_paths (required with it); a job that sets copy is run as secret output

copy_paths.description: SENSITIVE: effective regular files to copy to $OUT/layers-view/ with copy: true (up to 1000, never over an existing file). Refused unless the tool runs as a job run with secret_output: true

limit.description: Rows of the view shown inline (default 100); every row is in the paging file named in pages.view when there are more

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 60, at most 105): the layers not read are named and the answer is partial
